overallSummary: Fabio Giglietto maintains a strong and highly engaged academic presence across decentralized networks and professional platforms, with a total following of 3,580. His content focuses on computational social science, disinformation research, and academic career opportunities. Professional updates and research milestone announcements perform exceptionally well, with LinkedIn driving the highest absolute volume of interaction and Bluesky generating the highest relative engagement rates.

contentThemes.description: Announcements of new research papers and software updates, such as CooRnet v2.0, targeting coordinated inauthentic behavior.
Posts about recruitment for postdocs and PhD students, and major research grant wins.
Discussion of computational social science methods and upcoming presentations at niche conferences like DisinfoConf.

recommendations: Leverage Bluesky's high virality potential and active academic community by posting more frequent, interactive discussion starters on computational methods.
Utilize LinkedIn's professional reach for wider distribution of institutional milestones and recruitment drives, making sure to include clear, direct links to application portals.
Incorporate visual assets such as charts, model diagrams, or project logos to increase sharing rates on Mastodon and Bluesky.

platformInsights.bluesky: Bluesky is the most active platform in terms of relative engagement (6.14% average engagement rate), showing highly receptive audiences for research papers and academic recruitment with strong repost counts.
platformInsights.mastodon: Mastodon provides steady and targeted engagement (4.55% average engagement rate), proving highly effective for specific tool updates (CooRnet) and technical methodological discussions.
platformInsights.linkedin: LinkedIn has the largest follower base (1,850) and excels at professional network building, driving high volumes of likes and comments on organizational updates, grant awards, and job postings.

topPerformingContent.content: Just published our new paper on coordinated inauthentic behavior on social media platforms!
New research opportunity for PhD students interested in computational social science. Reply for details!
Excited to announce that our research team has been awarded a new grant to study information operations across social media platforms.
